items.title: Holman Bill — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He said, “Mr. Preminger, it wouldn‟t happen.” ... And Preminger said, a saxophone player telling him how to run his picture.

ctx.x: Yeah. Preminger and Giuffre. He said, “Mr. Preminger, it wouldn‟t happen.” Otto wanted them all to look back at Sinatra like that when he was screwing up, and Giuffre said, “It wouldn‟t have happened like that. We‟d have all looked down. We‟d have been embarrassed for the guy.” And Preminger said, a saxophone player telling him how to run his picture. Jack Montrose, that was the first movie music that he had ever played on. Midway through it, he turned to me, and he said, “Bill, this guy is a [?],” Bernstein,…

Then the other session that seems to be a monumental event was the recording of the complete Porgy and Bess. The people that I jotted down as being involved: Russ Garcia, Duke Ellington Orchestra, the Australian Jazz Quintet, Stan Levey group, recorded both in New York and Los Angeles. You‟re credited as playing clarinet on this, in addition.
